{{recipesummary | category = Potato recipes | servings = 4–5 | time = Prep: 50 minutes
Baking: 40 minutes
Total: 1 hour 30 minutes | difficulty = 2 | image = [[File:Potato_gratin_on_stove.jpg|300px]] }}{{recipe}} '''Potato gratin''' is a wonderful dish that is easy to make. It is a good accompaniment for [[Cookbook:Roast Lamb|roast lamb]] or [[Cookbook:Roast Chicken|roast chicken]], but is as delicious served on its own with a green salad. ==Ingredients== * 5 medium sized waxy [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], peeled or unpeeled * 4 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:chop|chop]]ped ([[Cookbook:Smoking|smoked]] garlic is good for this dish if you can get it) * ½ pint reduced fat [[Cookbook:Crème Fraiche|crème fraîche]], [[Cookbook:Cream|single cream]], or a mixture of semi-skimmed [[Cookbook:Milk|milk]] and crème fraîche * 3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] good quality [[Cookbook:Gruyère Cheese|Gruyère]], Challerhocker, or [[Cookbook:Emmental Cheese|Emmentaler cheese]], freshly [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]]. * 1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] * [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] (such as sea salt) and [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] * Fried [[Cookbook:Pancetta|pancetta]], [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]] cubes, or other cooked [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] (optional) ==Procedure== # Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to {{#invoke:Temperature|f|400}} # Slice the potatoes very thinly (about ⅛" thick), if possible using a [[Cookbook:Mandoline|mandoline]] to achieve evenness, and place them in some fresh water. # Swish around the potatoes in the water to get rid of the starch, because that excess starch can make the dish a little unpleasant. # Pour away the water and place the potatoes on a wooden surface. Then pat dry with a [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towel]] or kitchen towel, which is important because otherwise the remaining water will mix with the cream, causing curdling problems. # Return the sliced potatoes to a bowl and add the cream and chopped garlic. Add a generous [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of salt and some pepper. # You can also add a few fresh herbs ([[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]] is particularly good) but this is up to you. # Peel the zest of the lemon and add it to the mixture. # Mix well, so the cream gives a good coating to all the potatoes. # Pile the potatoes into a buttered, [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|oven-proof dish]]. The size is if course difficult to gauge but the potatoes should not be layered more than about 4 thick. # Grate a generous amount of cheese, and spread over the mixture. # Pop it all into the oven and leave until the top layer of cheese and potatoes are brown and the cream is bubbling and running down the side of the dish. This will take about 40 minutes. # For a final flourish before serving, grate a goodly amount of fresh [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]] over the cheese. == Notes, tips, and variations == * Some people tend to layer the potatoes in the heat proof bowl first and then pour the cream over. Some find this unreliable as the cream does not diffuse through all the layers, and the potatoes in a higgledy-piggledy pile in the bowl may be more attractive to some. * Swiss Appenzeller cheese is also a good choice. steps.text: Preheat the oven to
Slice the potatoes very thinly (about ⅛" thick), if possible using a mandoline to achieve evenness, and place them in some fresh water.
Swish around the potatoes in the water to get rid of the starch, because that excess starch can make the dish a little unpleasant.

Pour away the water and place the potatoes on a wooden surface. Then pat dry with a paper towel or kitchen towel, which is important because otherwise the remaining water will mix with the cream, causing curdling problems.
Return the sliced potatoes to a bowl and add the cream and chopped garlic. Add a generous pinch of salt and some pepper.
You can also add a few fresh herbs (thyme is particularly good) but this is up to you.
Peel the zest of the lemon and add it to the mixture.
Mix well, so the cream gives a good coating to all the potatoes.
Pile the potatoes into a buttered, oven-proof dish. The size is if course difficult to gauge but the potatoes should not be layered more than about 4 thick.
Grate a generous amount of cheese, and spread over the mixture.
Pop it all into the oven and leave until the top layer of cheese and potatoes are brown and the cream is bubbling and running down the side of the dish. This will take about 40 minutes.
For a final flourish before serving, grate a goodly amount of fresh nutmeg over the cheese.
